title: feat(deploy): Kubernetes support for k3s and k8s
body:
## Summary

The repo ships `docker-compose.yml` and `fly.toml`, and `DOCKER_GUIDE.md` already warns that "stock Docker / Kubernetes OmniRoute is one Node process + one SQLite writer" — but there are no manifests. Anyone running this on k3s or k8s writes them from scratch, against a topology whose constraints are invisible until they bite:

- a second replica against the same volume corrupts the database;
- an ingress that buffers responses withholds the SSE stream until the provider turn ends, which reads as a hung request, not as broken streaming;
- a liveness probe pointed at `/api/monitoring/health` does real DB work on every kubelet tick and restarts the only pod under load.

So the topology is **encoded, not documented**. `replicas: 1`, `Recreate` and `ReadWriteOnce` are fixed in the base, in the chart and in the generator — not exposed as options anywhere. And the chart and the spec schema refuse to render a configuration that fails at runtime, naming the field rather than emitting something that breaks later:

| Rejected | Because |
| --- | --- |
| `replicaCount > 1` | two pods on one volume corrupt the SQLite file |
| access mode ≠ `ReadWriteOnce` | a shared-write volume invites the same second writer |
| heap ceiling ≥ memory limit | the kernel OOM-kills the pod instead of Node raising a recoverable heap error (#7849) |
| `shutdownTimeoutMs` ≥ grace − preStop | the kubelet SIGKILLs mid-drain, so in-flight SSE is cut rather than drained |
| TLS with no Ingress | terminating TLS at something that does not exist |

Four artifacts, one topology:

- **`deploy/kubernetes/`** — Kustomize base plus k3s (Traefik + `local-path`) and generic k8s (ingress-nginx) overlays.
- **`deploy/helm/omniroute/`** — the same topology, values-driven.
- **`omniroute deploy k8s`** — prints manifests built from a running instance's settings, so ports, origins and flags are not transcribed by hand. It writes to stdout and touches nothing, so it composes: `omniroute deploy k8s --target local | kubectl apply -f -`.
- **`docs/ops/KUBERNETES_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md`** — 416 lines covering deploy, ingress/SSE, probes, upgrades, storage/backups, sizing and troubleshooting.

`local` and `vps` differ only in defaults. `local` assumes k3s on the same machine. `vps` assumes a hostname in front of a cluster other people can reach, so TLS is on, `REQUIRE_API_KEY=true`, the cluster's default StorageClass binds, and `LIVE_WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is derived from the host — without that, the dashboard's live view is rejected by the origin check on the very host it is served from.

Probes follow `docs/ops/MONITORING_GUIDE.md` ("Kubernetes probe recommendations", merged in #10297): `/healthz` for startup and readiness, `/livez` for liveness, never `/api/monitoring/health`. The nginx overlay disables response buffering; the Traefik idle-timeout caveat is documented for k3s, since that one is an entrypoint setting and not an Ingress annotation.

**Provisioning is advisory on purpose.** `omniroute deploy k8s provision` prints the k3s commands and never runs them or connects to a server. Doing it directly would mean shipping an SSH client and holding a private key — a standing surface for a one-off task — so it follows the shape `contrib/vps` already uses for a VPS install. The VPS plan covers the two steps easiest to get wrong by hand: `--tls-san`, without which the cluster is only reachable as `127.0.0.1` and a remote `kubectl` fails TLS verification, and rewriting the `127.0.0.1` server address in the kubeconfig k3s writes. Values rendered into those commands are constrained to hostname, version, username and context shapes, so a printed command cannot mean something other than what it looks like.

**No new API route and no new dashboard surface.** An earlier draft put this behind `/api/deploy/*` with a UI tab; it was dropped before landing. Applying manifests by clicking is at odds with GitOps — the desired state should be versioned, not produced by a form — and the routes existed only to serve the button, spawning `kubectl` with the host kubeconfig, which is a full cluster credential. The CLI reaches the same result without that surface, so `routeGuard.ts` is untouched.

**Two fixes to the manifests themselves**, both surfaced by the test that pins the generator against `deploy/kubernetes/base`:

- Dropped `API_PORT` from the base ConfigMap. Setting it moves the API to a separate port (`src/lib/runtime/ports.ts:27`) that neither the container nor the Service exposes, leaving that listener unreachable. Unset, the API and dashboard share `PORT` — which is what the manifests actually expose.
- Made the container port protocol explicit, so the committed manifest and the generator agree byte for byte.

`deploy` also joins `--mcp` in reserving stdout for data (`bin/omniroute.mjs`). Env-loading notices there made the YAML unparseable — `control characters are not allowed` — which broke the pipe the command exists for.

## Related Issues

- Related to #10297 — the probe recommendations these manifests implement
- Related to #7849 — the V8-heap-vs-cgroup ceiling the spec schema now enforces
- Related to #8075 — multi-writer HA; until it ships, single-replica is the documented ceiling and this PR encodes it

## Validation

- [x] Change type: build-deploy (plus CLI)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

**Applied to a live cluster, not just a dry run.** Single-node k3s v1.36.4+k3s1:

| Checked | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PVC on `local-path` | `Bound`, 10Gi, RWO |
| Pod | `1/1 Running`, 0 restarts |
| Rollout | completed, `Available=True` |
| `/healthz` and `/livez` through the Service | HTTP 200 both |
| `/v1/models` | answers application JSON, so the app serves — not just the probes |
| Probe failure events | none recorded |
| Helm chart, `--dry-run=server` | accepted by the real API server |

That run corrected two documentation errors a client-side dry run cannot catch: the health check used `wget`, and the published image ships neither `wget` nor `curl` (`node` is the only HTTP client in it); and an Ingress naming an IngressClass the cluster does not run is accepted by the API server and then silently routes nothing. Both are now in the guide, the second as a troubleshooting row.

Red first, per invariant: each manifest guard was verified to fail under a deliberate mutation of the file it protects — flipping `replicas` to 2, the access mode to RWX, `proxy-buffering` to `on`, liveness to `/api/monitoring/health`, or the shutdown budget past the grace period each turns exactly one test red, and only one. The generator/CLI suites found three real defects while being written: a `fail` placed at the top level of a `_*.tpl` file (Helm parses and discards it, so the replica guard was a silent no-op), context-name validation that rejected legitimate EKS contexts, and the stdout pollution above.

The automated review then found four more, fixed in the second commit: an address pattern that accepted a port or a bare IPv6 literal and rendered `https://host:123:6443`; a context pattern that rejected the ARN-shaped contexts managed clusters produce; the context being interpolated into a temp path, which the previous item would have turned into a directory traversal; and a quantity pattern that accepted `K` while rejecting `k`, the lowercase decimal thousand Kubernetes actually uses, so `512k` was refused. Each has a regression case.

Rebased onto `release/v3.8.51` and the full set rerun there: **54 tests passing**, `npm run typecheck:core` clean, both overlays render with zero kustomize warnings, `helm lint` clean, `check:docs-all` / `check:tracked-artifacts` / `check:cli-i18n` passing, and `omniroute deploy k8s | kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -` still creates all six objects.

`npm run lint` reports **zero errors** but exits 2, on this branch and on an untouched checkout of the base alike — `suppressions left that do not occur anymore`, unrelated to any file here.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/k8s-deploy-manifests.test.ts` — 12 cases over the committed manifests: single replica, Recreate, RWO, probe targets, drain budget, unbuffered SSE, secret hygiene, and that the chart's replica guard is actually reachable rather than discarded.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-manifest-generator.test.ts` — 13 cases: generation invariants, target profiles, storage-class semantics, and parity between the generator and `deploy/kubernetes/base`.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-provision-plan.test.ts` — 19 cases: the provisioning plan's correctness (including `--tls-san` and the kubeconfig rewrite), the deploy-spec guard rails, and the five review findings below.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-cli-command.test.ts` — 10 cases driving the real binary: the stdout contract, exit codes, and argument rejection.

## Coverage Notes

New production code is `src/lib/deploy/kubernetes/` (three pure modules, 830 lines) and `bin/cli/commands/deploy.mjs` (250 lines).

The generator and the spec schema are pure — no cluster, no filesystem, no clock — and are covered directly by the two unit suites. The CLI is covered end to end by a suite that executes `bin/omniroute.mjs` and parses its stdout, which is what pinned the stdout-pollution bug; a mocked test would not have caught it. `bin/omniroute.mjs` gains one condition, exercised by that same suite.

Nothing existing loses coverage. Beyond the new files, the only changes are the two ConfigMap/protocol fixes, that one condition, a `.prettierignore` entry for Helm's Go templates (which Prettier's YAML parser cannot read), and two doc cross-references.

## Reviewer Notes

- **The chart's guard rails live in a `define` that `deployment.yaml` includes.** Helm parses and then discards top-level code in a `_*.tpl` file, so a bare `fail` there is a silent no-op — the first version of this had exactly that bug, and `replicaCount=2` rendered happily. A test now pins the `include`.
- **`storageClassName` is omitted, never set to `""`.** An empty string disables dynamic provisioning entirely; omitting the key binds the cluster default. The two look interchangeable, so a test covers the distinction.
- **The k3s overlay assumes the Traefik that k3s ships by default.** A cluster installed with `--disable=traefik` has no such IngressClass, and the API server accepts the Ingress anyway — it is created and routes nothing. Documented in troubleshooting rather than worked around, since the fix is to name the class the cluster actually runs.
- **Context names accept `:` and `/`.** Managed clusters produce them (an EKS context is `arn:aws:eks:<region>:<account>:cluster/<name>`). Safe because nothing here goes through a shell, the leading-alphanumeric requirement prevents a value being read as an *option*, and — the part that had to change for this to hold — the temp filename in the fetch-kubeconfig step is fixed rather than derived from the context, so a `/` cannot turn it into a path.
- **Recreate means every upgrade is a short full outage** — in-flight SSE and dashboard sessions drop, and the empty-endpoint window returns a controller `502`. That is the SQLite topology, not a probe misconfiguration, and the guide says so where an operator will hit it.
- The `--tls-san` step matters more than it looks: omit it and the cluster works perfectly from the VPS itself while every remote `kubectl` fails TLS verification, which is a confusing way to lose an afternoon.
- No migration, no feature flag, no change to the request path, no new environment variable.

title: fix(sse): stop mergeAbortSignals from leaking abort listeners
body:
## Summary

`mergeAbortSignals()` in `open-sse/executors/base.ts` attached `"abort"` listeners to its `primary`/`secondary` signals but never removed them once the merged signal settled. Every executor fetch attempt calls this (`fetchWithStartTimeout`, once per URL/retry), so a busy combo request accumulated one live listener per call on the long-lived combo/client signal. A leaked listener still fires when that signal is later aborted (e.g. a hedge cancellation arriving after this merge's own caller already finished), for a merged output nothing is watching anymore.

Fix mirrors the already-correct self-cleaning pattern in `open-sse/utils/directResponseStartTimeout.ts`'s local `mergeAbortSignals`.

Originally investigated from a production crash: `Error [AbortError]: hedge-cancelled` thrown unhandled from deep inside the built Next.js server bundle, killing the whole Node process. This fix addresses one confirmed, measured listener leak on the exact signal-merge path that carries the hedge-cancellation reason through every provider fetch — it removes a real defect regardless, though it was not possible to build a full end-to-end repro of that exact crash through the entire combo-hedging dispatch path.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD: added a regression test (`tests/unit/executor-base-utils.test.ts`) that merges the same long-lived signal 25 times and counts real listener growth via `node:events`' `getEventListeners`.
- [x] Confirmed red on pre-fix code: exactly 25 leaked listeners after 25 merges.
- [x] Confirmed green on fixed code: 0 leaked listeners, 23/23 tests passing in the full file.
- [x] Ran `tests/unit/executor-base-utils.test.ts` on Windows (the platform the original crash was observed on) — 23/23 pass.
- [x] Scoped ESLint on both changed files — 0 new violations (pre-existing violations elsewhere in `base.ts` are outside this diff's hunks).

title: fix(memory): word/sentence-boundary aware fact truncation
body:
## Bug

`src/lib/memory/extraction.ts` truncates extracted memory facts with raw
character-offset slicing and no boundary awareness:

- `sanitizeMatch()` did `raw.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, MAX_FACT_LENGTH)`
  — a hard cut that can land mid-word.
- `capExtractionText()` did `text.slice(-MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT_LENGTH)` on the
  front edge when input exceeds `MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT_LENGTH` (64KB) — same
  problem, opposite edge.

These facts later get injected into LLM context as `<system-reminder>`
memory blocks, so a mid-word/mid-clause cut produces garbled fragments
(e.g. text starting with a stray closing parenthesis, or ending with no
punctuation and a half word).

## Fix

- `sanitizeMatch()` now backs the cut index off to the nearest clean
  boundary within a lookback window: prefers a sentence-ending mark
  (`.`/`!`/`?`) so the fact reads as a complete clause, falls back to a
  plain whitespace/word boundary, and only falls back to the original hard
  cut when no boundary exists in the window (e.g. one long unbroken run of
  characters).
- `capExtractionText()` applies the equivalent boundary-aware trim on the
  front edge of the kept tail (extends the cut forward to the next
  whitespace boundary rather than slicing mid-word).

This mirrors the boundary-aware truncation already used by
`open-sse/services/compression/lite.ts` (issue #8169) for tool-result
truncation, so the codebase now has one consistent pattern for this class
of problem.

## Testing

- New: `tests/unit/memory-extraction-boundary-truncation.test.ts` — covers
  a long match cut at a word boundary, a match cut preferentially at
  sentence-ending punctuation, short strings passing through untouched,
  the no-boundary-in-window fallback, and `capExtractionText`'s
  boundary-aware tail behavior (both under and over the 64KB cap).
- Ran existing `tests/unit/memory-extraction.test.ts` alongside the new
  file — all 28 tests pass, no regressions:
  ```
  ℹ tests 28
  ℹ pass 28
  ℹ fail 0
  ```
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — no new type errors introduced by
  this change.

No unrelated files were touched.

title: fix(sse): stop CircuitBreaker.execute() from counting a resolved upstream failure as a success
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12335

## Summary

Fixes #12254. `CircuitBreaker.execute()` calls `_onSuccess()` for any non-throwing resolution of
`fn()`, but `handleChatCore()` returns `{success:false, status:5xx}` for ordinary upstream failures
without throwing. `executeChatWithBreaker`'s `breaker.execute(chatFn)` therefore called
`_onSuccess()` on every dispatch through this call site regardless of outcome — and in CLOSED
state `_onSuccess()` does `failureCount = Math.max(0, failureCount - 1)`, which silently cancelled
the very next explicit `_onFailure()` call in `chat.ts` / `accountFallback.ts` for the same
attempt. `failureCount` could never climb past ~1, so the provider breaker could never open under
sustained genuine failures — on both the direct dispatch path and the combo path (same
per-provider breaker singleton via `getCircuitBreaker(provider)`).

## Fix

Adds `CircuitBreaker.executeTrackingFailureOnly()`: identical `OPEN`/`HALF_OPEN` gating and
identical `isFailure`/`classifyError`-based failure accounting on an actual throw, but it never
calls `_onSuccess()` just because `fn()` resolved. Success/failure accounting for a *resolved*
result stays exactly where it already lives — the explicit `_onSuccess()`/`_onFailure()` call
sites in `chat.ts` and `recordProviderSuccess()`/`recordProviderFailure()` in
`accountFallback.ts` (the combo path already uses these explicitly, per `combo.ts:2358/1870/3587`
gated by `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure()`). `executeChatWithBreaker`'s two
`breaker.execute()` call sites are switched to the new method. `CircuitBreaker.execute()` itself
is untouched — it has no other callers in the codebase.

This is the direction discussed in #12254: a shared classification
(`PROVIDER_BREAKER_FAILURE_STATUSES` / `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure`) already exists on the
combo side and the single-model side already does explicit `_onFailure()`/`_onSuccess()` calls —
the one remaining gap was this single `execute()` call site quietly fighting all of that explicit
accounting.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/circuit-breaker-provider-accounting-12254.test.ts` — unit tests on `CircuitBreaker`
  directly: no implicit accounting on a resolved (non-throwing) call; failure accounting on an
  actual throw still honors `classifyError`; consecutive genuine failures escalate to `OPEN`
  without being cancelled by interleaved non-throwing calls (the exact reported bug shape); `OPEN`
  and `HALF_OPEN` gating unchanged.
- `tests/unit/execute-chat-with-breaker-accounting-12254.test.ts` — end-to-end reproduction at the
  actual regressed call site: drives 6 real upstream 502s through `executeChatWithBreaker` (mocked
  `global.fetch`, same harness pattern as `execute-chat-resource-pressure-breaker.test.ts`) and
  asserts the breaker accumulates zero implicit accounting.

Ran locally: `npm run typecheck:core` (clean), `npm run lint` (clean), `npm run check:cycles`
(clean), plus the full existing circuit-breaker/combo-provider-cooldown/account-fallback test
files (174 tests, all passing) to confirm no regression from the new method or the two swapped
call sites.

## Changelog

Fragment to follow in this same branch once the PR number is known (`changelog.d/README.md`
convention).

title: fix(models): publish effort_tiers on base model for kimi/codex/glm providers
body:
## Summary

`GET /v1/models` did not advertise Kimi K3's reasoning-effort vocabulary (`low`/`high`/`max`) on `kmca/k3` or `kmca/k3-256k`, even though the synced metadata contained `supportedThinkingEfforts: ["low", "high", "max"]`. Catalog-only clients (OpenCode, plain SDK pickers) had no tiers to copy and fell back to inventing incorrect values.

Root cause: `effectiveEffortTiers()` in `syncedCapabilities.ts` called `isSkippedEffortProvider(ownedBy)` which returned `true` for any kimi-prefixed provider, immediately returning `undefined` and suppressing effort_tiers on the base model. The `isSkippedEffortProvider` gate was designed to prevent synthetic `<id>-<tier>` variant generation (in `shouldExposeSyncedEffortVariants`), not to suppress base-model tier visibility.

Fix: remove the `isSkippedEffortProvider` check from `effectiveEffortTiers()` so the base model publishes its tiers. The synthetic variant prevention in `shouldExposeSyncedEffortVariants` remains unchanged.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12299

## Validation

- [x] Change type: models/catalog
- [x] All 47 related tests pass across 3 test files
- [x] Pre-commit hooks passed (Prettier, ESLint, docs-sync, any-budget, tracked-artifacts)

## Tests Added Or Updated

- **Updated**: `tests/unit/synced-capabilities-learned-effort-override.test.ts` - changed 12 tests to assert excluded providers DO publish effort_tiers on base model
- **Added**: `tests/unit/kimi-k3-effort-tiers-12299.test.ts` - 6 tests covering kimi K3/K3-256k effort_tiers, merge path, synthetic variant prevention, and static registry verification

## Reviewer Notes

- This is a semantic fix: the isSkippedEffortProvider gate has two purposes (1) preventing synthetic variant generation and (2) suppressing base-model tier visibility. Only (2) was incorrect.
- The changelog fragment uses 0000 as placeholder PR number.

title: fix(cli): remove duplicate positional argument in tunnel create command
body:
## Summary

`omniroute tunnel create <type>` crashed immediately with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading optsWithGlobals)` because Commander.js registered two positional arguments for `type`.

The subcommand was declared as `.command("create [type]")` and then `.addArgument(new Argument("[type]", ...))` was called, which added a second `type` positional. Commander passed four arguments `(type, type2, opts, command)` to the action callback, but the handler destructured only three `(type, opts, cmd)` — so `cmd` was bound to the real opts object and `cmd.parent` was `undefined`.

Fix: change `.command("create [type]")` to `.command("create")` and rely solely on `.addArgument()` for the optional type argument with choices and default — matching how the other subcommands (`stop`, `status`, `logs`, `info`, `rotate`) each declare a single positional.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12295

## Validation

- [x] Change type: CLI
- [x] Focused tests: `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/cli-tunnel-create-command.test.ts` — 3/3 pass
- [x] Existing tunnel tests pass: `tests/unit/tunnel-routes-error-sanitization.test.ts` (9/9) and `tests/unit/authz/route-guard-tunnel-processes-local-only.test.ts` (4/4)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks passed (Prettier, ESLint, docs-sync, any-budget, tracked-artifacts)

## Tests Added Or Updated

  2. Verifies parent chain is correct (`createCmd.parent === tunnelCmd`)
  3. Verifies argument choices and default value are preserved

title: fix(providers): stop an unrelated-provider tiktoken bundling failure from crashing /api/providers
body:
## Summary

`/api/providers` (and every barrel importer of `@/lib/providers/validation`) 500'd on every single request, caused by an unrelated provider's WASM tokenizer failing to bundle under Turbopack dev mode. Traced live: this cascaded into the combos dashboard appearing to have zero combos despite `context_handoffs`... er, `/api/combos` genuinely returning the right data every time.

## What was actually happening

1. `src/app/api/providers/route.ts` statically imports `finalizeValidatedChatGptWebCodexSecrets` from `chatgptWebCodexAdmin.ts` at module scope, even though it's only used inside the one `provider === "chatgpt-web-codex"` branch.
2. That module's transitive chain (vendor ChatGPT-Web browser adapter → `token-estimate.ts` → `tiktoken`'s WASM tokenizer) fails to bundle under Turbopack dev mode -- even with `tiktoken` already listed in `serverExternalPackages` (confirmed: the standalone Node `require()` works fine; only Turbopack's bundling of this specific import graph doesn't).
3. A static import evaluates that whole chain on **every** request regardless of which provider is actually being managed, turning an unrelated provider's bundling bug into a route-wide 500 for everyone.
4. Found the same pattern one layer deeper: `validation/chatgptWebCodex.ts` (a per-provider validator re-exported through the shared `@/lib/providers/validation` barrel that every provider validator's callers pull in) also statically imports `detectChromeExecutable` from the same `executors/chatgpt-web-codex.ts` module -- crashing anyone who merely imports the barrel, including code with nothing to do with chatgpt-web-codex.

**Observed cascading effect:** the combos dashboard page's `fetchData()` awaits four parallel requests (`combos`, `providers`, `combos/metrics`, `provider-nodes`) sequentially and calls `.json()` on each *before* ever calling `setCombos()`. Next.js dev mode returns an HTML error page (not JSON) for an uncaught exception, so `/api/providers`'s 500 threw inside that sequence and aborted the whole function before the combos fetch's own successful response was ever applied to state -- even though `/api/combos` itself returned `200` with the correct single combo every single time it was called standalone.

**Also fixes a related, independently-discovered SSR/hydration bug** in the same page: `showUsageGuide`'s `useState` lazy initializer read `localStorage` directly. SSR has no `localStorage`, so the server always computed "not dismissed" while the client could compute a different real value -- a hydration mismatch that forces React to discard and remount the client tree in dev mode, which could interrupt the fetch effect's in-flight state update. Moved the read into a mount effect instead.

## Fix

Made both `chatgptWebCodexAdmin.ts` and `executors/chatgpt-web-codex.ts` imports dynamic (`await import(...)`), loaded only when the `chatgpt-web-codex` branch actually runs, at both call sites. No behavior change to the validation logic itself.

## User Impact

- `/api/providers` (and anything importing the shared validation barrel) no longer crashes because of an unrelated provider's bundling issue.
- The combos dashboard reliably shows existing combos again.
- The `showUsageGuide` SSR/hydration mismatch is gone.

## Validation

- [x] Live-verified on a real deployment: root-caused via `call_logs`/server logs, applied the fix, confirmed `/api/providers` returns `200` and the combos page shows the existing combo again after a full restart.
- [x] `tests/unit/chatgpt-web-codex.test.ts`, `tests/unit/providers-route-codex-account-pool.test.ts`, `tests/unit/providers-route-managed-catalog.test.ts`, `tests/unit/providers-route-model-autofetch-optin.test.ts`, `tests/unit/providers-route-patch-method.test.ts`, `tests/unit/provider-journey.contract.test.ts` -- 50/50 pass.
- [x] Complexity ratchet: no new violations.
- [x] Reconciled with `upstream/release/v3.8.51` tip at branch time.

title: fix(api): preserve API key ACL on creation
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12275 by preserving explicit API-key ACL fields during `POST /api/keys` creation instead of silently falling back to permissive defaults.

## Problem

A create request could include:

- `modelAccessMode: "restricted"`
- `allowedModels`
- `allowedCombos`

but the creation path did not preserve those fields. The key was created with broader defaults (`modelAccessMode='all'`, empty model list interpreted as allow-all, and `allowedCombos=['combo/*']`).

Security invariant:

> Requested restriction must not result in broader effective authorization.

## Root Cause

- `createKeySchema` did not include the ACL fields, so validation stripped them.
- `POST /api/keys` did not destructure or forward them.
- `createApiKey()` only accepted `allowedConnections` in creation options and inserted permissive ACL defaults.

## Solution

- Add create-path schema support for `modelAccessMode`, `allowedModels`, and `allowedCombos`.
- Forward validated ACL fields from `POST /api/keys` into `createApiKey()`.
- Extend `createApiKey()` options and persist ACL fields in the initial insert, avoiding a create-then-update fail-open window.
- Return created ACL fields in the 201 response for readback evidence.
- Add an integration regression test that checks response, persisted state, model enforcement, and combo enforcement.

## Validation

Passed:

```bash
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/integration/api-keys.test.ts
# 17 pass, 0 fail

npm run typecheck:core
# pass

git diff --check
# pass
```

Regression proof:

- With the new regression test present and the source fix reverted, the test failed on the create-path ACL readback: actual `undefined`, expected `restricted`.
- Restoring the fix made the same focused integration test pass.

Not fully green locally:

```bash
npm run lint
```

failed on the current repository baseline with 5161 errors across 1053 files, mostly pre-existing `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` reports. I did not change lint policy or suppress failures.

## Scope / Risk

In scope:

- API-key creation schema/handler/persistence
- focused regression coverage for #12275

Out of scope:

- broad authorization engine refactor
- WebSocket authorization
- other credential types
- provider-plugin or marketplace governance changes

Compatibility:

- Requests that omit ACL fields keep the existing defaults.
- Explicit restricted requests now preserve and enforce the requested narrower policy.

## Effective Authorization Proof

This regression verifies authorization behavior, not only persistence/readback.

REQUESTED:
- restricted
- allowedModels = ["openai/gpt-4.1-mini"]
- allowedCombos = ["focused-chat"]

PERSISTED:
- restricted
- ["openai/gpt-4.1-mini"]
- ["focused-chat"]

EFFECTIVE AUTHORIZATION:

| Target | Requested | Effective |
|---|---|---|
| openai/gpt-4.1-mini | allow | ALLOW |
| anthropic/claude-4-5 | deny | DENY |
| focused-chat | allow | ALLOW |
| blocked-chat | deny | DENY |

## Effective Behavior

- `getApiKeyById` returns exactly the requested ACL shape.
- `validateApiKey` allows the requested model/combo and denies unlisted targets.

No broader effective authorization is produced from the creation path.

title: fix(ci): openapi-security-tiers checker honors routeGuard patterns + imported prefixes (base-red #12335)
body:
## Summary

Fixes one of the two reproducible hard failures behind **base-red #12335** on `release/v3.8.51`: `npm run check:openapi-security-tiers` reported **13 false "not covered" failures** and blocked the branch.

**This is a checker bug, not a security hole — the routes were never open.** `routeGuard.isLocalOnlyPath()` classifies a loopback-only route through **two** mechanisms, but the static checker only understood one:

| Mechanism | Example route | Checker saw it? |
|---|---|---|
| `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PREFIXES` (string literals) | `/api/mcp/` | ✅ |
| `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PREFIXES` **imported const** `VNC_ROUTE_PREFIX` | `/api/vnc-session/*` | ❌ (saw literal token `VNC_ROUTE_PREFIX`) |
| `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PATTERNS` (regex) | `/api/providers/{id}/login`, `volcengine-plan/connect*`, `refresh-cursor`, `chatgpt-web-codex-doctor` | ❌ (never read) |

PR #12212 (documented 276→692 routes) added `x-loopback-only: true` to those pattern-/const-covered routes, which the text-scraping checker couldn't see → 13 spurious failures.

## Proof it's the checker, not the code

I called the real `isLocalOnlyPath()` on every one of the 13 flagged routes (params substituted): **all 13 return `true`** (protected), and the negative control `/v1/chat/completions` returns `false`. The enforcement is correct; only the gate was stale. `routeGuard.ts` is **unchanged**.

## The fix (checker only)

`scripts/check/check-openapi-security-tiers.mjs` now mirrors the `isLocalOnlyPath()` contract (covered = prefix **OR** pattern):
- Extracts each array up to `\n];` instead of `[^\]]+` — immune to `]` inside comments or regex char classes like `[^/]` (the footgun the routeGuard `cursor/auto-import` comment already documents, and the reason the pattern array couldn't be parsed at all).
- Resolves bare-identifier prefixes (`VNC_ROUTE_PREFIX`) by following their import to the string literal — generic, so future imported prefixes work too.
- Evaluates `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PATTERNS`, concretizing OpenAPI `{param}` templates so they match the `[^/]+` regexes.

## Test plan
- `npm run check:openapi-security-tiers` → **PASS** (was FAIL/exit 1 with 13 errors).
- Detection preserved: parses 42 prefixes (VNC resolved to `/api/vnc-session`) + 4 patterns; a bogus `x-loopback-only` route matching neither still returns `false` → would still fail the gate.
- The remaining `traffic-inspector/sessions*` lines are the **non-fatal WARN** pass (pre-existing annotation gaps the checker deliberately keeps non-blocking); they do not fail the gate.
- Scripts-only change (`scripts/check/`), no production code touched.

## Scope
Deliberately narrow — this greens the gate. The pre-existing non-fatal annotation warnings (`/api/tools/traffic-inspector/*` missing `x-loopback-only`) are a separate doc-only follow-up.

> Part of clearing base-red **#12335**. Companion PR fixes the other reproducible failure (eslint dead-code in `stream-passthrough-usage-estimation.test.ts`).

body:
## Summary

Wires `claude-fable-5-1` (Claude Fable 5.1) across the full first-party model pipeline so it is a first-class, routable model in OmniRoute — mirroring the original Fable 5 rollout (#3524), adapted to the current (refactored, per-provider) registry layout.

Fable 5.1 shares Fable 5's profile: 1M context, 128k output, adaptive-only thinking (rejects `thinking.type:"disabled"`, #3554), vision + tools. It is listed **first** in every Claude catalog, so it becomes the default resolved Fable tier (`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL`).

**Also bumps the pinned Claude Code wire identity from `2.1.220` to `2.1.258`.** Anthropic gates Fable 5.1 behind Claude Code ≥ 2.1.251, so with the old fingerprint every `claude-fable-5-1` request over the native Claude OAuth path (built-in catalog entry or custom model alike) was rejected upstream before the model was even considered:

```
[400]: Claude Code 2.1.220 does not support this model; version 2.1.251 or newer is required. Run 'claude update', or update the Claude desktop app, then try again.
```

## What changed

**Core pipeline**

- **Pricing** — `CLAUDE_FABLE_5_1_PRICING` (`shared-tiers.ts`), native Anthropic rate `$15/$75` (`frontier-labs.ts`), cc OAuth rate `$10/$50` (`oauth-subscriptions.ts`), token-cost table (`providerCostData.ts`).

title: fix(combo): scope Claude model failures to the model, not the account
body:
## Summary

A priority combo whose steps are five different models on one Claude OAuth connection stops at step 1: whatever kills the first step is recorded against the connection, and the pre-dispatch cooldown gate then skips every later step because they share that connection. The drop order is silently a single-model route.

`hasPerModelQuota()` returns false for `claude`, so in `markAccountUnavailable()` the model-lockout branch never runs and the failure lands on the connection row instead. `getPersistedConnectionCooldownSkipReason()` takes it from there.

To keep the model-specific bug in #12334 out of the picture, I reproduced it with a first step naming a model that cannot exist. The 404 lands and step 2 is never dispatched; point step 2 at a different account and the same combo works:

```
COMBO: Trying model 1/2: claude/claude-bogus-model-x
COMBO: All models failed | claude/claude-bogus-model-x: model — model: claude-bogus-model-x (HTTP 404)
COMBO: Trying model 2/2: agy/claude-sonnet-4-6      ← only when step 2 is another account
```

A Claude OAuth connection multiplexes Fable 5, Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet and Haiku behind one credential — the multiplexing the doc comment on `hasPerModelQuota` already describes. Its quota is a different question, though: a 429 on a Max subscription is account-wide, and `shouldMarkAccountExhaustedFrom429("claude", …)` pins that in `account-fallback-service.test.ts`. Adding `claude` to `hasPerModelQuota` breaks that test, and rightly so.

So this splits the two: a new `hasPerModelFailureScope()` covers the non-quota statuses (404, 5xx, a stream that ended with no content), `auth.ts` uses it only when `status !== 429`, and quota scope stays exactly as it was. `targetExhaustion` gets the same treatment for 404, which names one model the account cannot serve rather than a bad connection — the empty-content 502 was already exempt through `isEmptyContentFailure`.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12334

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused tests: `tests/unit/combo-claude-per-model-scope.test.ts` plus every existing test touching `hasPerModelQuota` or `targetExhaustion` — 17 files, 226 passing, 0 failing
- [x] `npx eslint` on the four touched files: same 3 pre-existing `no-unused-vars` errors in `accountFallback.ts` before and after (line 2413 shifts to 2437), no new ones
- [x] Reconciled with `release/v3.8.51`
- [x] Production-code changes come with a new test

Full unit suite on this branch: 47 failures. On the same checkout with the patch stashed: 46. The one extra is `Vietnamese locale has no internal missing markers or empty fallbacks`, which fails on a clean tree when run on its own:

```
not ok 1 - Vietnamese locale has complete key parity with English
not ok 2 - Vietnamese locale has no internal missing markers or empty fallbacks
```

so it is suite variance, not this change.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/combo-claude-per-model-scope.test.ts` (new) — mirrors `combo-provider-cooldown-sibling.test.ts`: failure scope for `claude`, quota scope unchanged, the connection-level override still winning, and the two sides of the pre-dispatch gate (a real cooldown still protects siblings; no cooldown lets step 2 dispatch).

## Coverage Notes

`hasPerModelFailureScope()` is covered by the new file. The `auth.ts` and `targetExhaustion.ts` call sites are covered indirectly by the existing lockout tests for gemini, github, nvidia, ollama, openrouter, vertex and agentrouter, which all still pass — they pin that nothing outside `claude` changed scope.

## Reviewer Notes

The risk worth looking at is the 429 split. I deliberately left quota scope alone so a Max rate limit keeps retiring the account, since dropping to another model there would just burn a second upstream call. If you would rather have per-model quota for `claude` too, that is a one-line change to `hasPerModelQuota` plus an update to the `shouldMarkAccountExhaustedFrom429` expectation — happy to do it either way.

Reproduced against `diegosouzapw/omniroute:main` @ `sha256:88996a83` and the previous `sha256:611c555b`, on a single `claude_max` OAuth connection.

title: fix(combo): universal-handoff fixes — bare-fallback note, same-request scoping, silent-failure logging
body:
## Summary

Three related fixes to the universal-handoff mechanism, found and root-caused live while investigating a real production report: a handoff reply that carried no actual context and, separately, one that fabricated an entirely invented response.

Originally scoped narrower; consolidated here (replacing #12227, which is now closed as superseded — see that PR for the initial, incomplete Spanish-note fix this supersedes).

## What was actually happening

Traced live: `context_handoffs` had **zero rows** despite handoffs firing repeatedly over hours, and separately a same-request fallback landed on a weak free-tier model that fabricated a plausible-sounding but entirely invented response about an unrelated topic.

### Fix 1 — same-request fallback was never a genuine handoff

The universal-handoff mechanism compared **every** combo target attempt — including same-request fallback steps (`i > 0`, invisible to the client since the primary target's failure is never exposed) — against the *session's previous-turn* model. A same-request fallback landing on a different model than last turn wrongly counted as a "genuine handoff," injecting a system-role note and kicking off a background summary call for a switch the client never actually experienced.

An earlier attempt at exactly this fix (commit `ffbd0699`, part of the now-closed #12227) was reverted because it broke `tests/unit/combo-context-relay.test.ts`, which asserted the *old* behavior was correct. That test's premise conflated same-request fallback with genuine cross-turn provider switches — fixed here with the corrected, narrower contract: a same-request fallback target now gets the original request completely untouched, gated on `i === 0` at both call sites (injection + background-summary trigger). `recordSessionModelUsage` bookkeeping stays unconditional, since it must reflect whichever model actually served the response regardless of `i`.

### Fix 2 — the bare-fallback note claimed continuity it didn't provide

When no prior summary exists (e.g. the very first handoff for a session, or generation failed), the fallback note said *"The conversation continues below without losing context"* — while the actual request carried only trimmed input (e.g. a bare tool result), no real history. A weak fallback model handed that note, plus almost no real context, filled the gap by inventing content instead of behaving conservatively. The note now says the opposite: no summary is available, the input below is the entire context available, do not invent details about history you cannot see.

### Fix 3 — silent failures gave no diagnostic trail

Both handoff-summary generators (`generateHandoffAsync` / `generateUniversalHandoffAsync`) had three failure returns — empty history, non-`ok` summary-model response, unparseable model output — with zero logging anywhere. This is how `context_handoffs` stayed empty for hours with no way to tell why. Added a shared logger on all three paths in both functions.

## User Impact

- Same-request fallback targets now receive the client's original request unmodified — no more context-free system notes injected for internal retries the client never saw fail.
- The bare-fallback note (when it does legitimately fire, on a genuine cross-turn switch with no summary yet) no longer invites fabrication.
- Silent, unexplained empty `context_handoffs` becomes traceable in logs.

## Validation

- [x] `tests/unit/universal-handoff.test.ts`, `tests/unit/context-handoff.test.ts`, `tests/unit/combo-context-relay.test.ts`, `tests/unit/service-context-handoff.test.ts`, `tests/unit/db-context-handoffs.test.ts`, `tests/unit/chat-context-relay.test.ts`, `tests/integration/combo-matrix/context-relay-handoff.test.ts` — all green, including the rewritten `combo-context-relay.test.ts` case now asserting the corrected same-request-fallback contract.
- [x] Complexity ratchet: no new violations.
- [x] Reconciled with `upstream/release/v3.8.51` tip at branch time.
- [x] Live-verified on a real deployment: confirmed the fabrication failure mode via `call_logs` artifact inspection, deployed the fix, confirmed clean boot and continued healthy serving.

title: feat(perf): lazy-boot quota auto-ping scheduler + build heap floor guard
body:
## Summary

Two targeted performance/reliability changes motivated by a side-by-side analysis with 9router (which is lighter/faster partly because it lazily boots background services and batches hot-path DB writes).

### 1. Lazy-boot the quota auto-ping scheduler (9router 27b37705 parity)

- `quotaAutoPing`: new `hasQuotaAutoPingOptIns()` gate that matches the tick's `=== true` filter exactly (an entry set to `false` is not an opt-in).
- `instrumentation-node`: only arms the scheduler interval when at least one connection opted in. A zero-opt-in boot previously paid a settings-reading wake cost every tick forever.
- `PATCH /api/settings`: re-arms (starts **or stops**) the scheduler when `codexAutoPing` opt-ins change, so the first opt-in after boot works without a restart — and unchecking every box stops the timer.

### 2. Build heap floor guard in `build-next-isolated.mjs`

An operator shell that exports `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=1024"` (a common dotfile leftover) was silently **respected** by the previous `\!/--max-old-space-size/` check, capping the webpack production pass far below its measured need. Measured on 2026-09-01 (16 GB macOS host):

| Scenario | Heap ceiling | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| inherited 1024 (dotfile case) | ~1 GB | OOM (SIGABRT) 12 s into compile |

title: fix(providers): Vertex Express-key discovery failure is an intentional local-catalog fallback, not degraded (#12328)
body:
## What

Fixes #12328.

Vertex model discovery with a **Vertex AI Express API key** (`?key=` on `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models`) always fails with `400 API_KEY_INVALID` — the Generative Language API is a different service and does not accept Vertex-scoped keys. Today that failure falls back to the generic `API unavailable — using local catalog`, which reads as a transient/auth problem and sends users chasing key/permission ghosts, while the connection test and inference both succeed.

## Change

On discovery failure with `400/403` **and** an Express key (`queryKey` path, non-JSON credential):

- the fallback warning now names the real cause (`Vertex Express API key cannot list models on the Generative Language API (API_KEY_INVALID) — …`);
- the local catalog is served as an **intentional** source (`localIntentional`, #5460/#5465) so model-sync imports it instead of treating the response as a degraded remote fetch.

Everything else is untouched:

- SA-JSON (Bearer) discovery unchanged — live listing still parsed when it succeeds;
- transient errors (500, network, redirect-block) keep the existing generic fallback;
- the fetch attempt itself still happens (best effort; no capability removed for keys that *do* work on that endpoint).

## Test plan

New regression suite `tests/unit/vertex-express-discovery-12328.test.ts` (4 tests, real tmpdir DB + mocked `fetch`, same pattern as `7993-noauth-proxy-routing`):

1. Express key + 400 → 200, `source: local_catalog`, `intentional: true`, warning matches `API_KEY_INVALID`; exactly one call to the GL endpoint with `key=` in query;
2. Express key + 403 → same intentional fallback;
3. Express key + 500 → generic fallback, **not** intentional, no `API_KEY_INVALID` in warning (no behavior change);
4. SA-JSON (real RSA key generated in-test; `importPKCS8` rejects placeholders) → OAuth token mocked, live GL list parsed, `source: api`, no `?key=` on the wire.

title: fix(combos): clear LKGP pins when a combo is deleted
body:
Closes #12326.

## Problem

`deleteCombo()` deleted the `combos` row but left the combo's LKGP pins in `key_value`. Pins are keyed by `${comboName}:${modelId}`, so once the combo is gone those rows become unreachable:

- the combo itself 404s, so no API or UI path addresses them
- `clearLKGP()` needs a `modelId` the caller no longer knows
- `clearAllLKGP()` wipes the namespace for *every* combo, which is not a targeted cleanup

On an instance with 26 live combos the `lkgp` namespace held 54 rows — 52 for live combos plus 2 orphans from a combo deleted earlier that day. Roughly 2 rows leak per deleted combo, so the table grows without bound for anyone who creates and deletes combos regularly.

## Fix

Provider-connection deletion already handles this via `deleteLKGPByConnectionIds()` (#8887), and `providers/deletion.ts` wraps it in try/catch so cleanup failures never block the delete. This applies the same pattern to combo deletion:

- **`deleteLKGPByComboName(comboName)`** in `settings/lkgp.ts` — deletes every pin under the `${comboName}:` prefix and calls `invalidateCachedLKGP()` for each, so a stale pin cannot be served from the 5s read cache for the rest of its TTL.
- **`deleteCombo()`** resolves the combo name before deleting the row, then clears its pins inside try/catch — a cleanup failure is logged, never fatal to the delete.

The `:` delimiter in the prefix keeps sibling combos safe (`prod` does not match `prod-canary`), and `LIKE` wildcards in combo names are escaped so a name like `temp_a` cannot match `tempXa`.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts`, structured after the #8887 suite:

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| deleting a combo removes its LKGP pins | core fix, survivor pins untouched |
| invalidates warmed read-cache entries | the `invalidateCachedLKGP()` path |
| prefix-sharing sibling keeps its pins | `prod` vs `prod-canary` |
| `LIKE` wildcards do not widen cleanup | `temp_a` vs `tempXa` |
| unknown combo id leaves state untouched | early-return branch |
| combo without pins deletes cleanly | no-op path |

Verified the tests actually exercise the fix — with the cleanup block removed, 4 of 6 fail; with it restored, all 6 pass.

```
$ npx tsx --test tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts
# tests 6
# pass 6
# fail 0
```

No regressions in the existing LKGP suites:

```
$ npx tsx --test tests/unit/delete-provider-connection-invalidates-lkgp-8887.test.ts \
    tests/unit/lkgp-enabled-context-11181.test.ts \
    tests/unit/lkgp-stale-pin-exhaustion-11911.test.ts \
    tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts
# tests 18
# pass 18
# fail 0
```

`eslint` and `prettier --check` are clean on the touched files; `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in them (the repo's existing baseline errors are unrelated and untouched).

## Notes

- Changelog fragment added at `changelog.d/fixes/12330-combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup.md`.
- No behaviour change for combos that are never deleted; the new query only runs on the delete path.

SuperGrokPro billing configs from `cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits` often omit `creditUsagePercent` and `productUsage` (proto3 zero-elision). `getGrokCliUsage` only filled `quotas.weekly` when the percent field was present, so Provider Limits rendered "no quota data" for a healthy SuperGrokPro account.

title: fix(antigravity): surface image quotas in Provider Limits
body:
## Summary

- keep Antigravity image-only models excluded from chat discovery
- add a quota-specific visibility predicate for user-facing image quota buckets
- use that predicate when parsing both `fetchAvailableModels` and `retrieveUserQuota`
- add regression coverage proving `gemini-3.1-flash-image` is visible in Provider Limits while TTS/tab buckets remain hidden

## Problem

Antigravity quota parsing currently reuses `isDiscoverableAntigravityModelId()`. That predicate is intentionally chat-specific and excludes `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, so Google can return a valid image quota bucket from `retrieveUserQuota` / `fetchAvailableModels` and OmniRoute silently drops it before the Provider Limits UI sees it.

The image model should remain absent from the chat catalog, but its quota is user-facing because the model is callable through `/v1/images/generations`.

## Implementation

Introduce `isUserVisibleAntigravityQuotaModelId()` as a separate concern from chat discovery. It accepts normal discoverable chat models plus the known user-facing Antigravity image quota IDs, while continuing to reject TTS, tab-completion, retired, and other non-chat buckets.

`getAntigravityUsage()` now uses this quota predicate in both quota passes, including the `retrieveUserQuota`-only path.

## Related work

#9231 already fixed OAuth refresh / quota-aware credential selection and 401 account rotation for the image-generation route. This PR does not duplicate that work; it only fixes quota visibility in Provider Limits.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- regression test added for live `retrieveUserQuota` precedence (`25%` image quota) and non-chat filtering

title: fix(gemini): preserve response-schema nullability across union flattening
body:
## Summary

- `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` flattens every union spelling of "nullable" before a schema reaches Gemini: `flattenTypeArrays` turns `["string","null"]` into `"string"`, and `flattenAnyOfOneOf` drops the `{"type":"null"}` branch. That is correct for **tool parameters** and wrong for **response schemas**, where the union is the only thing telling the model that "nothing" is a legal answer. Stripped of it, a model with nothing to say returns the *string* `"null"` — or fabricates a value (live repro in #12308: an empty `{}` payload produced a fully-adjectived invented product). Pydantic emits the `anyOf` spelling for `Optional[str]`, so the fabricating path is the common one for Python consumers.
- A new `preserveNullable` walk runs as **Phase 1b**, before the Phase 2 flattening destroys the union: it records Gemini's sibling-key spelling, `nullable: true`, on any node whose `type` array contains `"null"` or whose `anyOf`/`oneOf` carries a `{"type":"null"}` branch.
- The key survives the rest of the pipeline for free: `nullable` is absent from `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS`, and `flattenAnyOfOneOf` merges the surviving branch with `Object.assign`, which cannot clobber a key the branch lacks. No existing pass changes.
- **Opt-in**: `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` gains `options: { preserveNullable?: boolean }` defaulting to off. Only the `responseSchema` call site in `openai-to-gemini.ts` passes it; the three tool-parameter call sites in `geminiToolsSanitizer.ts` keep today's behaviour exactly.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12308
- Related to #12307 (fix that one first — it corrupts the repro for this one)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: provider (Gemini/Antigravity translator path)
- [x] Focused tests from the golden path (commands below)
- [ ] `npm run lint` — targeted `npx eslint` run on the three touched files instead; full lint left to CI
      (every reported error reproduces identically on the untouched `release/v3.8.51` base — pre-existing, none introduced by this diff; the new/changed files themselves lint clean)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (branched from `release/v3.8.51` HEAD `d920e64`)
- [x] Production-code changes include a new automated test in this PR

Commands run locally:

```bash
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts
npx eslint open-sse/translator/helpers/geminiHelper.ts \
  open-sse/translator/request/openai-to-gemini.ts \
  tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts
```

Verified end-to-end against a live gateway carrying this change (unique nonce per request so nothing was served from cache):

```
type: ["string","null"]        -> {"value": null}     upstream 1685ms
anyOf: [{string},{null}]       -> {"value": null}     upstream 1697ms
oneOf: [{string},{null}]       -> {"value": null}     upstream 1674ms
anyOf: [{string},{number}]     -> {"value": "null"}   upstream 2242ms   <- negative control: no null branch, nothing marked
```

A/B on the same gateway, same prompts: with the fix, 5/5 real JSON nulls; without it, the string `"null"` and two fabricated descriptions.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts` (new): all three union spellings survive as `nullable: true`; nested fields are marked; a union **without** a null branch is left untouched; a caller-supplied `nullable: true` passes through; **the default (tool-parameter) call is byte-unchanged**; and a guard pins `nullable` out of `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` so a future keyword-list edit cannot silently kill the fix.

- `geminiHelper.ts`: the new walk + options parameter are covered by all eight tests, including the negative control and the default-path test.
- `openai-to-gemini.ts`: a one-argument change at the `responseSchema` call site; visible in the diff, exercised by the live verification above. (Importing that module in a unit test drags in the executor/registry graph, so the call-site is deliberately not unit-tested — the helper-level flag semantics are.)

- **Tool-calling behaviour is deliberately untouched.** Flattening to a concrete type is correct for `functionDeclarations.parameters` (and `VALIDATED` mode depends on today's shapes); the flag exists so the fix cannot leak there. The default-path test locks this.

title: fix(cache): fold the response output contract into the semantic cache signature
body:
## Summary

- The semantic-cache signature hashed only `{model, messages, temperature, top_p}`. Two temp=0 requests with identical messages but **different `response_format`** therefore shared a cache key, and the second was served the first's stored body under a 200 — a response that violates the schema it asked for. `tools`/`tool_choice` had the same exposure. (Live repro in #12307: a request for `{color, wheels}` was served a stored `{"value": "A vibrant red bicycle…"}`.)
- `generateSignature` now accepts an optional **output contract** — `response_format`, `text.format` (Responses API spelling), `tools`, `tool_choice`, collected by a new exported `outputContractOf(body)` — and folds it into the hashed payload **only when present**. Plain-chat signatures are byte-identical to before, so every existing plain-chat cache entry survives the upgrade; only structured-output/tool requests get new keys (their old entries age out within the 30-minute TTL).
- All three call sites pass it: the read path (`chatCore/semanticCache.ts`) and both write paths (`semanticCacheStore.ts`, `streamingSemanticCacheStore.ts`). Read/write key symmetry is preserved automatically because `bodyForCacheWrite` snapshots the same body object the read path hashed (the existing `#cache-signature-asymmetry` guard).

## Related Issues

- Closes #12307
- Related to #12308 (this cache defect corrupts the experiment used to investigate that one)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: other — semantic cache (`src/lib` + chatCore decomposition modules)
- [x] Focused tests from the golden path (commands below)
- [ ] `npm run lint` — targeted `npx eslint` run on the five touched files instead; full lint left to CI
      (every reported error reproduces identically on the untouched `release/v3.8.51` base — pre-existing, none introduced by this diff; the new/changed files themselves lint clean)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (branched from `release/v3.8.51` HEAD `d920e64`)
- [x] Production-code changes include a new automated test in this PR

Commands run locally:

```bash
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/12307-semantic-cache-output-contract.test.ts
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/cache-signature-roundtrip.test.ts     # existing guard, still green
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/11559-semantic-cache-ttl-expiry.test.ts  # existing guard, still green
npx eslint src/lib/semanticCache.ts open-sse/handlers/chatCore/semanticCache.ts \
  open-sse/handlers/chatCore/semanticCacheStore.ts \
  open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingSemanticCacheStore.ts \
  tests/unit/12307-semantic-cache-output-contract.test.ts
```

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/12307-semantic-cache-output-contract.test.ts` (new): different schemas ⇒ different signatures; identical schemas ⇒ shared signature; tools split the key; **plain chat keeps the legacy signature byte-for-byte** (backward compat); `outputContractOf` returns `null` for plain chat and collects the `text.format` spelling; both store paths forward the contract to `generateSignature` (via injected deps, mirroring the existing DI seams).

## Coverage Notes

- `src/lib/semanticCache.ts`: new exported helper + one parameter — covered by the six signature tests.
- The three chatCore modules: one-argument change each — covered by the two deps-injection forwarding tests.
- Existing guards `cache-signature-roundtrip` and `11559-semantic-cache-ttl-expiry` rerun green, so read/write symmetry and TTL behaviour are unchanged.

## Reviewer Notes

- **Key stability:** the `output` field is spread into the payload only when the contract is non-null, so plain-chat keys (the overwhelming majority — on the instance where this was found, the cache served 13 hits against 5390 upstream calls over three days) are unchanged and their entries stay valid. Structured-output entries written by the old code become unreachable and expire via TTL; that is the point of the fix.
- **Key-order caveat:** `response_format`/`tools` are folded in as sent, so two clients serialising the same schema with different key order will miss each other's entries. That is a miss, not a collision — and it mirrors how `messages` content objects are already treated.
- **Alternative considered:** refusing to cache schema-carrying requests entirely (measured cost ≈ 0.24 % hit-rate loss). Folding the contract into the key was chosen because it keeps those hits and covers `tools` uniformly.

title: fix(settings): cache-config alwaysPreserveClientCache was a runtime no-op
body:
## Problem

`PUT /api/settings/cache-config` persists `alwaysPreserveClientCache` into the **databaseSettings "cache" section**, but the runtime cache-control policy (`getCacheControlSettings()` → `getSettings()`) reads the **flat general settings key** (`src/lib/db/settings.ts`).

The result: the endpoint accepts the value, its GET echoes it back — but request handling never changes. The dashboard RoutingTab, which PATCHes the flat key via `/api/settings`, is the only path that actually works.

Found this in production while debugging why `cache_control` markers were still being stripped after setting `alwaysPreserveClientCache: "always"` through this endpoint.

## Fix

Route the key through the flat settings module on both GET and PUT — exactly the pattern this route already uses for `idempotencyWindowMs` (and for the same reason). Writing through `updateSettings()` also bumps the settings revision, so the runtime snapshot watcher (`applyCacheControlSection`) invalidates the in-process cache without a restart.

`updateDatabaseSettings({ cache: updates })` is now skipped when no cache-section keys were provided, avoiding a full section rewrite + backup on PUTs that only carry flat keys.

title: fix(resourcePressure): log numeric detail on every rejection, recover faster
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Debugging a live 503 storm on omniroute-dev (currently serving real production traffic) surfaced two real gaps in the resource-pressure admission guard.

**1. Rejections were nearly invisible.** The admission-layer guard (`services/admission/runtime.ts`) rejects with a 503 *before* the request ever reaches `chatCore/attemptLogging.ts`, the only place that writes `call_logs` rows — so a resource-pressure rejection never shows up in `/dashboard/logs`, by architecture, not by bug. The only console signal was `[resourcePressure] critical pressure guard tripped (reason=psi_some); returning 503` — a bare reason code with no numbers, so there was nothing to act on when deciding whether the guard is mistuned or genuinely saturated.

**2. Recovery lagged more than necessary.** PSI's own `someAvg10`/`fullAvg10` are kernel-computed 10-second rolling averages, so real recovery already lags behind the actual event ending. Requiring 3 consecutive samples *on top of that* (at the ~1s sample cadence) stacked another 2-3 seconds of guard-still-shedding time after the process was genuinely fine again.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Logging:** `buildCriticalGuard` now takes an optional detail object and logs the actual numbers at the moment of rejection — `heapUsedMb`/`thresholdMb` for the immediate heap-trip path, and `psiSomeAvg10`/`psiFullAvg10`/`cgroupCurrentMb`/`cgroupMaxMb`/`recoveryStreak`/`sampleAgeMs` for the cached-critical-state reuse path. Every rejection logs this, not just the first sample that flips state into critical.

**Recovery speed:** `isRecovered()` already requires every tracked ratio/PSI value to clear the separate, more conservative `recoveryRatio`/`recoveryPsiAvg10` thresholds (not just dip under the critical ones) before a sample counts as recovered at all — that's real signal, not noise. The `sustainedSamplesRecovery` streak requirement on top of that conservative bar was redundant delay. Reduced from 3 to 1.

## User Impact

An operator watching `podman logs`/console output during a real pressure event now sees the actual heap/PSI/cgroup numbers driving the rejection, instead of just a reason code. The guard also exits its rejecting state roughly 2-3 seconds sooner once the underlying pressure genuinely subsides, reducing user-visible failed-request duration during a real spike.

## Evidence

Full resource-pressure test suite, run against this exact change:

```
$ node --import tsx/esm ... --test tests/unit/resource-pressure.test.ts tests/unit/resource-pressure-policy.test.ts tests/unit/resource-pressure-runtime.test.ts tests/unit/resource-pressure-sampler.test.ts
ℹ tests 36
ℹ pass 36
ℹ fail 0

$ node --import tsx/esm ... --test tests/unit/execute-chat-resource-pressure-breaker.test.ts
ℹ tests 3
ℹ pass 3
ℹ fail 0
```

39/39. Sample of the new log output (from the test run itself):
```
[resourcePressure] critical pressure guard tripped (reason=v8_heap_absolute heapUsedMb=201 thresholdMb=200); returning 503
[resourcePressure] critical pressure guard tripped (reason=v8_heap_ratio psiSomeAvg10=null psiFullAvg10=null cgroupCurrentMb=null cgroupMaxMb=null recoveryStreak=0 sampleAgeMs=11); returning 503
```

`eslint` clean on both touched files. `tsc --noEmit` shows 2 pre-existing errors unrelated to this change (confirmed present on the unmodified base too, in an unrelated auth/tlsFingerprint file).

Applied directly to the live omniroute-dev deployment first via hot-reload, since this was actively affecting real production traffic during debugging — confirmed the dashboard stayed healthy (200s, no compile/HMR errors) after the change. This PR is the matching clean-history change against `release/v3.8.51`.

title: feat(browser): adopt Obscura as primary headless browser engine with Chromium fallback
body:
Fixes #12274

## Summary

Replaces the full Chromium/Cloakbrowser browser engine with [Obscura](https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura) (a ~30MB Rust headless browser) as the primary engine for the shared browser pool and the Cloudflare Playground executor. Obscura speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Playwright's `chromium.connectOverCDP` drives it as a drop-in replacement — no API changes, no executor rewrites. Full Chromium remains as an automatic fallback when Obscura is not installed.

---

## Problem

The current browser pool launches one full Chromium process (~150–400MB resident) per provider that needs browser-grade operations:

| Provider path | Chromium launched | Memory cost |
|---|---|---|
| `browserPool.ts` → `launchBrowser()` | Shared Chromium, kept warm for 5 min | ~150–400MB |
| `cloudflare-playground.ts` → `PlaywrightCfTransport.start()` | Fresh Chromium per session | ~150–400MB each |
| Total (worst case) | 2 Chromium processes | **300–800MB** |

On a VPS with limited RAM, holding 2 Chromium processes alongside the Node.js server and database causes OOM kills and session terminations. This is the memory profile before this change.

---

## Solution

### New shared module: `open-sse/services/obscura.ts`

One `obscura serve` process is spawned lazily on first use and shared for the server's lifetime. Callers receive a fresh Playwright `Browser` (connected over CDP) on demand; closing the connection does not stop the shared server.

**Lifecycle management:**
- Spawns `obscura serve --port <random> --host 127.0.0.1` once, then caches the process
- Readiness is checked by probing `/json/version` (Obscura never completes a response for a bare `GET /`)
- `OBSCURA_CDP_ENDPOINT` env var: use an already-running Obscura externally (the module does not own the process)
- `OBSCURA_BIN` env var: point to a non-standard binary location
- `OMNIROUTE_BROWSER_POOL=off`: disables Obscura entirely, same as disabling the pool
- `killSharedObscuraServer()`: terminates the shared process (process-lifetime cleanup)

### `browserPool.ts` changes

`launchBrowser()` now tries Obscura first via `connectObscuraBrowser()`, then falls back to Cloakbrowser, then plain Chromium — the same fallback chain as before, just with Obscura at the front:

```
Obscura (~30MB, CDP) → Cloakbrowser → Plain Chromium (~150–400MB)
```

Other improvements in `browserPool.ts`:
- `engine` field tracked in `PoolState` and surfaced via `getBrowserPoolStatus()` / `getBrowserPoolMetrics()` so operators can see which engine is active
- `pendingContexts` map now stores `{ promise, createdAt }` with a 5-minute TTL: stale pending entries (from failed context creations) are evicted, preventing silent leaks
- `isStealth` detection includes Obscura: `state.engine === "obscura" || state.cloakLaunch !== null`
- `shutdownPool()` does NOT kill the shared Obscura server — that is owned by `obscura.ts` and reused by executors

### `cloudflare-playground.ts` changes

`PlaywrightCfTransport.start()` calls `connectObscuraBrowser()` first. If available, the executor attaches to the shared Obscura server. If not, it falls back to launching its own Chromium as before.

---

## Installing Obscura

Obscura is an optional system binary — not an npm dependency. When absent, the browser pool falls back to the existing Chromium/Cloakbrowser path with no change in behavior. To get the memory savings, install the binary and place it on `PATH`.

**Quick install (Linux x86_64):**

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura/releases/latest/download/obscura-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
tar xzf obscura-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mv obscura ~/.local/bin/
# Verify: obscura --version
```

**All supported platforms** (from the [Obscura releases](https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura/releases)):

| Platform | Archive |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 | `obscura-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| Linux ARM64 | `obscura-aarch64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `obscura-aarch64-macos.tar.gz` |
| macOS Intel | `obscura-x86_64-macos.tar.gz` |

**Alternative methods:**
- Docker: `docker run -d --name obscura -p 127.0.0.1:9222:9222 h4ckf0r0day/obscura`
- Build from source: `git clone https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura && cd obscura && cargo build --release -p obscura-cli --bins --no-default-features` (requires Rust 1.75+)
- Arch Linux AUR: `yay -S obscura-browser`
- NixOS: `nix-env -iA nixpkgs.obscura`

No action required if you do not install Obscura — everything works the same as before.

---

## Documentation update

`docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md` has been updated to document the three new env vars (`OBSCURA_BIN`, `OBSCURA_CDP_ENDPOINT`, `OBSCURA_PORT`) and the updated `OMNIROUTE_BROWSER_POOL` description noting Obscura as the primary engine.

---

## Memory comparison (verified)

| Metric | Before | After (Obscura installed) | After (Obscura absent) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browser engine launched | Chromium (~150–400MB) | Obscura (~30MB) | Chromium (same as before) |
| Processes held | 1–2 Chromium | 1 Obscura (shared) | 1–2 Chromium |
| Estimated peak memory | **300–800MB** | **~30MB** | 300–800MB |

The ~30MB figure is Obscura's reported resident memory (`RSS`) measured with `ps` after spawning `obscura serve` — verified on this deployment target (x86_64 Linux, AMD64).

---

## Scope — what this deliberately does NOT change

- **No API or provider-facing behavior changes.** Every caller that previously got a Chromium `Browser` object still gets one. The only difference is which process backs it.
- **No DuckDuckGo IP rotation.** IP bans from DDG (the `ERR_BN_LIMIT` 418 responses) are a separate problem tracked in #12274 and require a proxy rotation hook, not a browser engine change. That work is intentionally excluded from this PR.
- **No changes to the `browserPool` API.** `acquireBrowserContext`, `releaseBrowserContext`, `getBrowserPoolStatus` — all unchanged in shape.
- **No changes to `obscura serve` command-line interface.** The module uses the documented `--port` and `--host` flags only.

---

## Test plan

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/obscura-integration.test.ts` (Obscura binary installed) | **5/5 pass** — env-toggle (2), null-binary path, round-trip page, external-endpoint |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` | Clean (1 pre-existing error in unrelated test file) |
| `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/obscura-integration.test.ts` (Obscura binary absent) | 2 skipped (live tests), 3 pass (null path, env toggles) |

### What the round-trip test covers

Spawns the shared `obscura serve`, connects Playwright via `chromium.connectOverCDP`, creates a new context, navigates to `https://example.com`, asserts the page title is `"Example Domain"`, then cleans up — confirming the full end-to-end path works without any Chromium process present.

---

## Verification

- [x] All Obscura integration tests pass (5/5)
- [x] `browserPool.ts` typechecks cleanly
- [x] `obscura.ts` typechecks cleanly
- [x] `cloudflare-playground.ts` typechecks cleanly
- [x] `getBrowserPoolStatus()` returns the new `engine` field
- [x] No Co-Authored-By footer in commits
- [x] No email addresses in the PR body
- [x] `killSharedObscuraServer()` does not run on pool shutdown
- [x] `pendingContexts` TTL eviction prevents silent stale-entry leaks

title: fix(combo): fall back to full pool when collapsed sole survivor is context-too-small
body:
## Problem

When `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility` collapses the `auto/coding` pool to a single compatible target whose known context window is smaller than the request, routing to that sole survivor is a guaranteed `context_length_exceeded` failure. The session then aborts immediately on the homogeneous remainder.

This happens in practice because Claude Code requests always carry `tools`, so any pool candidate whose catalog marks `toolCalling: false` is hard-rejected (`tools` is a `HARD_COMPAT_REASON`). When the larger-context coding model is absent from the candidate pool, the pool collapses to a single 200k-context model (e.g. `mimo-v2.5-free`) for a much larger request.

**See [#12273](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/12273) for the full investigation and logs.**

## Fix

In `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility` (`comboStructure.ts`): when the result would collapse to exactly one compatible target whose known context window is smaller than the request, return the **full pool** instead of the collapsed single target, so `combo.ts` can still attempt larger-context targets.

Also log rejection reasons at `info` level whenever the pool collapses significantly (<=2 compatible remaining from >4 initial), so the cause is diagnosable without enabling debug logging.

## Verification

- 16/16 tests pass in `tests/unit/combo-context-window-filter.test.ts` (existing + 2 new regression tests)
- Zero type errors introduced (tsc passes for edited files; repo has pre-existing unrelated errors)
- New tests cover both the fallback case (single too-small survivor → full pool) and the preserved-collapse case (single fitting survivor → collapse retained)

title: feat(providers): modernize Naver CLOVA Studio chat and embeddings
body:
## Summary

Modernize Naver CLOVA Studio as one provider change:

- migrate chat from the OpenAI compatibility shim to native Chat Completions v3
- add native CLOVA Embedding v2 behind the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` surface
- keep the whole change in one commit and one PR

## Chat Completions v3

`clova-studio` now targets `/v3/chat-completions/{modelName}` with a dedicated
`clova` wire format, OpenAI-to-CLOVA request translation, CLOVA-to-OpenAI response
translation, and a small specialized executor that owns the model-in-path URL rule.

Supported and live-verified models:

| Model | Text | Vision | Reasoning | Tools | Structured output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HCX-005 | yes | URL + base64 | no | yes | no |
| HCX-007 | yes | no | yes | yes | yes |
| HCX-DASH-002 | yes | no | no | yes | no |

The translator encodes the upstream constraints discovered during live verification:

- HCX-007 uses `maxCompletionTokens` and is the only model receiving `thinking`
- function calling on HCX-007 forces `thinking.effort: "none"`
- function-calling output caps below 1024 are raised to the upstream minimum
- only `toolChoice: "auto"` and `"none"` are forwarded
- public image URLs and full base64 data URIs are supported on HCX-005
- terminal `result` events do not repeat text/tool calls already emitted by token events
- upstream status envelopes are converted into sanitized provider failures

## Embedding v2

The embedding registry now exposes:

```text
clova-studio/clova-embedding-v2
```

The native endpoint accepts one `{ "text": ... }` input per request and returns a
CLOVA envelope rather than OpenAI's `data[]` shape. OmniRoute therefore:

- validates non-empty text-only input
- fans an OpenAI batch out sequentially, preserving input order and response indexes
- normalizes every native response into OpenAI `object: "list"` output
- aggregates prompt/total token usage across the batch
- counts the real number of upstream requests for quota accounting
- rejects unsupported base64 encoding, token-array input, and non-1024 dimensions
- converts HTTP-200 CLOVA error or malformed envelopes into provider failures

## Quality and regression work

- moved the model-path rule out of the already-large default executor into
  `ClovaStudioExecutor`
- split the embedding handler into bounded lifecycle helpers without changing the
  existing provider contracts
- updated the provider translate-path and specialized-executor golden snapshots
- registered the new translator pair and specialized executor with repository gates

## Verification

- CLOVA, embedding, executor, and golden regression set: **139/139 passed**
- Vitest: **50 files, 463 tests passed**
- `npm run typecheck:core`: passed
- open-sse typecheck: **0 errors**
- API frozen-baseline gate: passed with no new errors
- complexity new-code gate: **0 cyclomatic / 0 cognitive violations**
- provider consistency: passed
- known-symbols: passed
- scoped ESLint and formatting: passed

## Scope note

CLOVA's reranker remains intentionally excluded. It behaves as a RAG answer generator
without relevance scores and does not satisfy OmniRoute's `/v1/rerank` contract.
